questions.question: What was the historical proposal from the Quraysh leaders that prompted the revelation of Surah Al-Kafirun?
options: That the Prophet would pay tribute in exchange for the right to preach in Mecca
That the Prophet and Quraysh would take turns worshipping each other's gods, each for a year
That the Prophet would leave Mecca permanently in exchange for safe passage
That the Prophet would marry into a Qurayshi clan to seal a political alliance
questions.explanation: The tafsir explains that the surah was revealed when Qurayshi chiefs such as Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-As ibn Wa'il, Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf proposed that the Prophet worship their idols for a year in return for them worshipping his God for a year. The surah is the unequivocal divine refusal of that compromise.

questions.question: True or false: The verse uses 'ma' (what) rather than 'man' (who) to refer to the objects of pagan worship, subtly underlining their unreality as deities.
questions.explanation: Layer 1 notes this linguistic precision is intentional: calling the idols 'what' rather than 'who' strips them of any illusion of personhood and underlines their inadequacy as objects of worship, since they are inanimate statues with no true divine reality.

questions.question: According to the foundational explanation, the famous closing phrase 'For you is your religion, and for me is my religion' is best understood as which of the following?
options: A declaration that all religions are equally valid paths to God
An endorsement of religious syncretism in worship
A statement of personal accountability and principled separateness, not approval or equivalence
A command for Muslims to permanently sever all social contact with non-Muslims
questions.explanation: The tafsir clarifies that 'lakum dinukum' uses the possessive to indicate accountability and consequence, not approval. Each party owns and is answerable for their own path. It is principled separateness with no forced conversion, not religious relativism.

questions.question: True or false: Ibn Kathir in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim describes Surah Al-Kafirun as 'the surah of disavowal' (bara'ah) from shirk, and reports that reciting it has been described as freeing one from polytheism.
questions.explanation: Layer 2 cites Ibn Kathir directly: he calls this surah the surah of bara'ah from shirk and connects it to the prophetic statement that whoever recites it has freed himself from shirk. He also reports that the Salaf considered it equivalent in reward to a quarter of the Quran.

questions.question: Which classical scholar offered the detailed grammatical reading that the active participle 'abidun' in verse 4 elevates the denial from behavioral to ontological, meaning the Prophet is not merely refusing an act but is constitutionally incapable of being what the polytheists want him to become?
questions.explanation: Layer 2 attributes this analysis to Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb, who argued that 'abidun' as a nominal form indicates essential nature, making verse 4 a deeper and more final declaration than verse 2 about who the Prophet fundamentally is.

questions.question: True or false: According to Ibn Uthaymeen, the Prophet's habit of pairing Surah Al-Kafirun with Surah Al-Ikhlas in the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr shows that this declaration of exclusive worship was meant to be a regular daily spiritual practice, not merely a one-time political statement.
questions.explanation: Layer 3 cites Ibn Uthaymeen on this point: Al-Ikhlas establishes what Allah is (the One), while Al-Kafirun establishes what the believer does with that knowledge, directing worship exclusively to Him. Reciting them daily renews the heart's clarity about its fundamental commitment.

questions.question: How does Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir characterize the stance the surah takes in its final verse?
options: It endorses religious relativism, the view that all religions are equally valid paths
It endorses religious coexistence and tolerance while rejecting religious relativism
It is abrogated by later Medinan verses on jihad and no longer applies
It applies only to those specific Qurayshi leaders and has no contemporary relevance
questions.explanation: Layer 3 explains al-Zuhayli's careful distinction between three concepts: Islam endorses tolerance and coexistence (no compulsion in religion) but rejects relativism (the idea that all paths are equally valid). Verse 6 endorses peaceful coexistence without abandoning the truth claims of tawhid.
